newsitem.title: USA: Xerox sees new products adding to '97 revs.
newsitem.headline: Xerox sees new products adding to '97 revs.

text.p: Xerox Corp said Tuesday it expects its new family of digital copiers -- the first of which were rolled out in a major product launch last week -- to contribute to 1997 revenue growth.
Xerox said that in two weeks, it will roll out important new digital production publishing and printing products, both color and black and white, as part of its new digital line.

In Q1, it said, digital product revenues were 31 percent of total revenues and grew 18 percent, reflecting excellent growth in color copying and printing and strong growth in high-speed laser printing and production publishing.

This growth in the first quarter came despite some customer anticipation of the new product rollout. Xerox also said that its DocuColor 40 copier, which it said is the industry's fastest color document production system at 40 pages per minute, was an important contributor to growth.

Black and white light lens copiers, its non-digital product line, now 55 percent of its total revenues, fell two percent in the first quarter. Strong copier equipment sales in the U.S. were largely offset by declines in Europe and Brazil.
"I am optimistic about out outlook," said Xerox Chairman and CEO Paul Allaire, in a statement.
